channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 37 studies found very low certainty evidence that it is unclear whether reduced spinal range of motion independently predicts pain intensity, disability, or global recovery in people with specific or nonspecific spinal pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Mirror therapy versus functional electrical stimulation cycling in post-stroke lower limb rehabilitation: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: An RCT comparing mirror therapy (MT) and functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling (FES-C) as adjuncts to conventional rehabilitation for subacute stroke found both effective, with greater improvements in FMA-LE scores compared to control (MT: MD -2.60, p=0.004; FES-C: MD -3.00, p=0.008), and FES-C also significantly improved Brunnstrom stage and SS-QOL.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of iTBS and rTMS Combined with Robotic Rehabilitation on Ambulation and Lower Extremity Motor Function in Chronic SCI Patients.
item.description: A single-blind RCT (n=30) found that both rTMS and iTBS combined with robotic rehabilitation improved lower-extremity motor function (LEMS: rTMS median +4.0, iTBS +5.0 vs sham +0.0; SCIM III: rTMS +3.0, iTBS +5.0 vs sham +0.0) and ambulation (10 MWT: rTMS +6.6, iTBS +5.7 vs sham +0.7) in chronic incomplete SCI patients at 4-week follow-up, with no significant differences between active groups.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing lower extremity muscle stiffness after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
item.description: A systematic review of 6 studies (173 ACLR participants) found reduced passive vastus medialis shear modulus in operative limbs (Hedges' g -1.10 to -1.21 vs controls), associated with quadriceps strength, knee function, and landing biomechanics. Semitendinosus stiffness was reduced after hamstring tendon harvest (g -1.29 to -1.64).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Return to Performance Continuum for Football (Soccer) Players After ACL Reconstruction: Bridging Rehabilitation, Return to Play and Sustained Performance.
item.description: This paper outlines a staged return-to-performance continuum for football players after ACL reconstruction, emphasizing a structured transition from return-to-sport clearance to sustained performance. It integrates on-field rehabilitation, team training, competitive match play, and early/sustained return to performance through four pillars: movement quality, technical/tactical re-training, physical reconditioning, and neuromuscular performance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: Early isometric quadriceps strength LSI at 3 months post-quadriceps tendon autograft ACL reconstruction (QT-ACLR) strongly predicted 2-year IKDC scores, highlighting the importance of early strength recovery for long-term outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Percutaneous Electrolysis for the Management of Musculoskeletal Disorders. A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 trials found that adding percutaneous electrolysis (PNE) to therapeutic exercise for tendinopathies was not superior to sham or exercise alone for pain or function. In tendinopathies, PNE combined with TE showed greater short- and medium-term pain reduction compared to dry needling plus TE, but no functional superiority. No significant differences were found between PNE and dry needling for pain or function in myofascial pain syndrome.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical performance clustering as a marker of frailty, fall risk, and cognitive health in older adults
item.description: A study of 368 older adults used unsupervised classification of 23 physical performance measures (PPMs) to identify three distinct clusters (High, Moderate, Low Physical Performance), which significantly stratified individuals by frailty and fall risk, with muscular power and joint moments being the most discriminative features.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Calf Injuries: An Anatomy-Based Approach to Diagnosis, Management and Return to Sport.
item.description: This review discusses an anatomy-based approach to diagnosing, managing, and returning to sport after calf injuries, emphasizing precise characterization of myoconnective structures. It highlights that current evidence for linking anatomical patterns to prognosis is limited, and rehabilitation should be function-led with multifactorial return-to-sport decisions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Identifying heterogeneous patterns of real-world upper limb use beyond motor severity: a cross-sectional sensor-based study in people with subacute stroke
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 101 subacute stroke patients identified six heterogeneous upper limb activity patterns beyond motor severity using accelerometers and clinical assessments. Key distinguishing factors included motor function tests (ARAT), Motor Activity Log, upper limb inattention, and paretic-side dominance, suggesting personalized rehabilitation should consider factors beyond motor deficits.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: The effects of route previewing on adaptive gait and gaze behaviour under cognitive dual-task conditions in older adults
item.description: A study with 39 older adults found that route previewing attenuated negative effects of cognitive dual-tasking on adaptive gait, reducing stepping errors and cross-steps (p < .001) and improving gaze behavior, suggesting value for visual-planning interventions.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: In adolescent patients after patellar stabilization surgery, higher ACL-RSI scores (≥59.2) were significantly associated with successful return to sport, even after adjusting for sex.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of office-based vergence/accommodative therapy with movement for accommodative dysfunction in concussion-related convergence insufficiency: a secondary analysis of the CONCUSS randomised clinical trial
item.description: Immediate office-based vergence/accommodative therapy with movement (OBVAM) was highly effective in remediating accommodative dysfunction associated with concussion-related convergence insufficiency compared to watchful waiting.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Efficacy and evidence certainty of traditional Chinese exercises for musculoskeletal disorders: an umbrella review of meta-analyses
item.description: High-certainty evidence supports the efficacy of Traditional Chinese Exercises (TCEs), particularly Tai Chi, for musculoskeletal disorders, with optimal benefits observed from sustained interventions (≥6 months, ≥3 times/week).
item.author: BJSM

item.title: The Role of Psychosocial Factors in Returning to Physical Activity and Sport Among Female Football Players After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury: A Scoping Review
item.description: A scoping review of seven studies found that psychosocial factors significantly influence female football players' return to physical activity and sport after ACL injury. Barriers included uncertainty, fear, lack of confidence, and poor social support, while facilitators were confidence, motivation, strong social support, and athletic identity.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Dextrose prolotherapy for chronic symptomatic rotator cuff tendinopathy and subacromial bursitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 studies (13 RCTs, 1 observational) found very low certainty evidence that dextrose prolotherapy may have little to no benefit for chronic symptomatic mixed rotator cuff tendinopathy and/or subacromial bursitis, and may result in worse physical performance compared to corticosteroid injections.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Patients' experiences of participating in physiotherapeutic telerehabilitation for postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction; a qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study of 14 women in Sweden found that telerehabilitation for postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction was perceived as a complementary approach, improving accessibility and continuity of care, despite concerns about the absence of physical examination and hands-on guidance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: First aggression as a planning signal in post-acute stroke rehabilitation: Service benchmarks, goal setting, and a 60-day precaution window from a comprehensive observational cohort.
item.description: A retrospective observational cohort study (N=1683) found that the first electronic health record-documented aggression after stroke signals longer length of stay (+17.9 days) and lower functional independence measure (mFIM) efficiency/effectiveness, warranting a 60-day precaution window for rehabilitation planning.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association between hospital-level factors and early rehabilitation initiation in patients with acute ischemic stroke: a multilevel analysis using a Japanese administrative database from a rural prefecture.
item.description: A multilevel analysis of 17,194 patients with acute ischemic stroke in Japan found that provision of weekend rehabilitation services was significantly associated with early rehabilitation initiation (incidence rate ratio 1.65), while therapist staffing levels and stroke volume were not.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The enhanced rehabilitation programme for significant musculoskeletal injuries from the manchester arena bombing - A process evaluation study investigating patients' and physiotherapists' experiences.
item.description: A process evaluation of the Enhanced Rehabilitation Programme (ERP) for major trauma survivors found it beneficial for physical and psychological recovery, though participants noted challenges with long-term sustainability and transition back to standard NHS care, suggesting resource limitations and systemic constraints as adoption barriers.
item.author: PubMed
